main_body: A hide or panel stretched in a wooden frame, with a thick brown bottom rail and two short legs below it
top_band: none: the top is only a 1-2 row dark brown frame edge at rows 0-2, then yellow hide from row 3 down. No lighter horizontal surface is visible from above.
evidence: Reading the middle column: dark frame rim at rows 0-2, then about 14 rows of yellow hide with blue marks (rows 3-16). That block is a vertical panel seen face-on, or at best a flat slab seen from above, and it has no foreshortened top band. Below it come a brown bottom rail (rows 17-20) and legs (rows 21-24). The frame's horizontal beams show no top faces, and there is no front-edge line or eave shadow. The rail and legs sit under a large flat panel, so this is a front elevation (or a top-down slab) rather than a 3/4 frame.

style.evidence: The outline is dark brown beside the wooden frame, not black. The yellow hide has a few tones with blue pattern marks and dark dots, and the brown frame has about 3 steps. That is less ramp depth and fewer colours per tile than the cheese stall or the roofed well, but it is not a flat sticker.
